summary: Iteration 13: Client Calendar Review & Override + Workout Status Rename verification. BACKEND: 15 passed / 3 xfail — POST/GET/DELETE /api/calendar/day-override work end-to-end. Auth guard (401 without token), enum & tag validation (invalid day_type/equipment/training_preference silently dropped, custom: tags accepted), created_at preserved on update, DELETE clears + adds 'cleared' history entry, GET returns history DESC. Regression: /api/calendar/timeline, /api/roster/jobs/active, /api/coach/videos, /api/coach/analytics, /api/exercises/video, /api/roster/upload-and-generate, /api/workouts/regenerate all still 200/expected. FRONTEND (420x900): client login -> Calendar renders 7 month cards with cal-day-YYYY-MM-DD grid; DayEditModal opens with ALL required testIDs (tag-sick, tag-poor_sleep, tag-no_gym, dt-sick, av-30, eq-bodyweight, pref-reduce, apply-week, dayedit-notes, dayedit-save, dayedit-close); chips highlight in crimson when tapped; save closes modal cleanly; reopening restores notes+chips+shows CLIENT · entry in CHANGE HISTORY. cal-fab-add opens modal on today. Long-press on a day WITH a workout opens the modal (short-press correctly navigates to workout details). Workout details renders new status-coach_reviewing badge near the date; ZERO occurrences of standalone 'PENDING' as a workout status on the workout page. Coach /clients -> client-card -> /coach/client/{id} loads; ZERO 'REVIEW' plain-text occurrences (replaced by StatusBadge component). Coach desktop 1440x900 /overview sidebar (Overview/Clients/Calendar/Approvals/Library/Videos/Messages/Analytics/Profile) intact — no regression. FLAG: seed DB has duplicate workout rows for many (user_id, date) pairs (74 dates observed, up to 7 copies), which surfaces a latent backend bug where POST /calendar/day-override uses find_one+update_one and may flip status on a stale duplicate — the client-facing workout id shown by /calendar/timeline may not receive the status change. Not a new regression from this iteration, but likely to bite in production.

minor.issue: Uses find_one + update_one for workout status flip. When the DB has duplicate workouts for the same (user_id, date) — currently 74 such dates — only ONE duplicate is flipped, and /calendar/timeline may surface a DIFFERENT duplicate that still reports status=null. Result: user saves the modal, gets no visual feedback on the calendar cell / workout screen because the wrong row was mutated. Fix: use update_many({user_id, date, coach_locked:{$ne:true}, completed:{$ne:true}}, {$set:{status:...}}) AND upstream de-dupe of the workouts collection.

db.workouts contains 74 dates with duplicate rows for user_id 62f90680-... (client@crewfit.com) — up to 7 rows on 2026-03-02. Likely accumulated across successive regenerate/generate-month runs that insert without cleaning old rows for the same date. See RCA in report.

action_items: HIGH: Fix duplicate-workout data corruption. Add a unique index on (user_id, date) in db.workouts AND de-duplicate existing rows (keep the most recent per pair). Then switch /calendar/day-override to update_many so any surviving row updates atomically.
MEDIUM: Consider making /calendar/day-override also stamp override_id on the affected workout(s) so the UI can show 'client edited this day' without a second round-trip.
LOW: The DayEditModal has no confirmation summary; per spec this is intentionally deferred. When implemented later, add a 'Ready to build your plan?' summary sheet before dispatching.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 3294 lines (guideline: <=700). Split calendar/override/roster/workout routers into separate modules.

DayEditModal.tsx line 118: coach_locked branch triggers Alert.alert then still calls onSaved()+onClose() unconditionally — acceptable for MVP but the user may not realise the change was suppressed on their workout. Consider showing a persistent inline warning in the header when reopening a coach-locked day.

StatusBadge.tsx deriveStatus() maps w.status=='pending' to 'coach_reviewing' — good backward-compat shim; document this so backend authors don't accidentally re-introduce a raw 'pending' status label.

workout/[id]/index.tsx line 94 uses native alert(m.desc) — works on web but on native iOS/Android this shows a browser-style alert which is inconsistent with the rest of the app; consider Alert.alert(m.label, m.desc) for parity.
The custom: tag prefix is accepted in the backend but no UI path exists yet to enter a custom tag string — this is dead code today until the ADD CUSTOM TAG affordance is built.

rca_of_issue: Latent bug — RCA: /api/calendar/day-override (server.py L1237-1245) fetches the target workout via db.workouts.find_one({user_id, date}) then update_one({id: wk.id}, ...). MongoDB find_one is non-deterministic when multiple documents match. Meanwhile /api/calendar/timeline uses an aggregation that may surface a DIFFERENT duplicate for the same (user, date). If the two picks disagree, the client sees stale status on their calendar despite a successful save. Reproduction: (1) log in as client@crewfit.com, (2) tap 2026-07-01 (which has 3 workout rows), (3) POST /calendar/day-override tags=[sick], (4) GET /workouts/1ab3eda2-... (the id returned by timeline) — status is still None. But GET /workouts/9ef53042-... (a sibling duplicate) shows status=coach_reviewing. Mitigation: (A) unique index db.workouts.create_index([('user_id',1),('date',1)], unique=True) + de-dup migration keeping the latest row per pair, (B) change update_one -> update_many in the override handler.
